advances: An auxiliary paired original cap-cost obstruction for unequal homothetic triangles. The upper certificates do not identify the exact paired minimum or the mixed depth of a three-fiber source.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The point is interior to both triangles. In the scale-$r$ triangle the barycentric coordinates, multiplied by $r$, are $r-L,L/2,L/2$; the scale-$s$ triangle has the analogous list. Since $L\ge2s/3>2r/3$, the two smallest entries are $r-L,L/2$ and $s-L,L/2$, respectively, with ties harmless. Applying 431423848c9bacf8 Part 1 and using areas $r^2V,s^2V$ gives depths $2VL(r-L)$ and $2VL(s-L)$.

Use $u=(1,1)$ and $t=L-s$. The thresholds are $2L-s$ and $s$. The first satisfies $0<2L-s<r$, and the second is the zero-area supporting edge of the larger triangle. A cap of the triangle $R T$ cut at diagonal threshold $q\in[0,R]$ has area $V(R^2-q^2)$, by subtracting the lower homothetic triangle. Thus the exhibited sum is $V[r^2-(2L-s)^2]$, whose difference from the ordinary-depth sum is $V\Delta$. Move the first threshold up by $\varepsilon=\Delta/(8s)$ and the second down by $\varepsilon$. They still sum to $2L$ and are both strictly interior to their respective support intervals, since $\varepsilon<r+s-2L$ and $\varepsilon<s$. The cost increase is
$$
V\big(4(s-L)\varepsilon-2\varepsilon^2\big)\le4Vs\varepsilon=V\Delta/2.
$$
At $L=2s/3$ the ratio reduces to $(3r+s)/(4s)$ and tends to $3/4$ along the allowed scales. Since the infimum is no larger than the exhibited value at each such scale, the upper restriction on a universal lower factor follows.

In the stated rational case the supporting thresholds are $4/9,4/3$, yielding $65V/81$. Taking $t=-1/3$ instead gives $5/9,11/9$, both strictly proper, with respective areas $56V/81,23V/81$. The ordinary depths are $16V/81,64V/81$ by the same identity. All boundary lines are null for planar area.
statement: Let $T=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)\}$ have area $V=1/2$. Take $0<r<s<3r/2$, $2s/3\le L<r$, and let $A=rT$, $B=sT$, $y=(L/2,L/2)$. For $u\ne0$ and $t\in\mathbb R$ use the two actual closed caps with common normal $u$ and thresholds $u\cdot y+t$ on $A$, $u\cdot y-t$ on $B$. Write $p_{A,B}(y)$ for the infimum of the sum of their areas and $f_A(y),f_B(y)$ for the ordinary raw depths. Then $f_A(y)+f_B(y)=2VL(r+s-2L)$. Put $\Delta=(s-r)(r+s-2L)>0$. One such cap pair costs $f_A(y)+f_B(y)-V\Delta$, and one with both traces proper costs at most $f_A(y)+f_B(y)-V\Delta/2$. For $L=2s/3$ the point is the larger centroid, and the first exhibited cost divided by $f_A(y)+f_B(y)$ is $(3r+s)/(4s)\to3/4$ as $s/r\uparrow3/2$. Hence every universal lower factor for this class is at most $3/4$. For $r=1,s=4/3,L=8/9$ the ordinary sum is $80V/81$ and explicit supporting and proper pairs cost $65V/81$ and $79V/81$.
title: Unequal homothetic triangles can fall below the sum of their ordinary depths
